title: 5040 and other Anti-Prime Numbers - Numberphile
summary: Numberphile's James Grime discusses highly composite numbers, nicknamed anti-primes, which have more factors than any smaller number, using 5040 as the central example. It touches on Plato and Ramanujan.
why: HN points to it whenever highly divisible numbers matter, such as sharding, base 12, time units and music.
